description: From-scratch graph-native learning and control of an aerial body through opaque stabilized actuator commands and raw three-dimensional pose receipts.

microtheory.name: aerial_adaptation
microtheory.description: Discover a three-dimensional action model by intervention, then fly toward a graph-held spatial goal.

rules.name: aa_measure_flight_state
rules.comment: Three-dimensional distance, takeoff, and success are graph assessments over raw pose. The host only records the verdict.

rules.name: aa_choose_motor_babble
rules.comment: Intervene on every opaque command before using a learned consequence. Ordering is graph-held and conveys no actuator semantics.

rules.name: aa_choose_learned_flight_action
rules.comment: Choose the opaque command whose learned three-dimensional consequence leaves the smallest goal residual. At the goal, choose the empirically quietest consequence. No command direction is imported.

rules.name: aa_open_flight_trial
rules.comment: Materialise the selected opaque action and graph prediction before the simulator is touched.

rules.name: aa_learn_aerial_forward_model
rules.comment: Update the selected opaque command's three-dimensional consequence from a verified simulator receipt, entirely in graph state.

rules.name: aa_close_frozen_flight_trial
rules.comment: Close a receipt-backed trial after plasticity is frozen without changing its AerialActionModel.

rules.name: aa_detect_direct_control_emergency
rules.comment: Infer the failed CF2X motor quadrant after angular motion exceeds the declared diagnostic evidence threshold, then latch the current position as the reduced-attitude hold target.

rules.name: aa_direct_three_rotor_reduced_attitude_control
rules.comment: Compose raw surviving-motor RPM in graph state at sensor rate. Yaw is deliberately relaxed; roll, pitch, position, and altitude are controlled through constrained CF2X force allocation.

rules.name: aa_expose_motor_decision_option
rules.comment: Initialize each opaque AerialActionModel in the shared collapse vocabulary. The hard flight preparation rule projects the existing three-dimensional cost at each decision epoch.
